reality_delta: Real changes occurred: metadata verification is now automatic and semantic at write time with hard dispatcher failure on mismatch, the codex-hook self-check covers additional read vectors, and live Codex tests confirmed blocking of cat and python3 -c open(...) raw reads while allowing metadata reads. However, these improvements do not yet include independent validation of Kimi agent constraints, and live hook coverage was demonstrated for only two of the claimed blocked vectors.
main_concern: The main AI successfully patched the specific gaps flagged in the previous review—replacing opt-in verification with mandatory write-time checks and expanding hook detection—but may be treating 'self-check passes and two live blocks' as full infrastructure readiness while still lacking independent proof that the Kimi provider is actually bounded, and without live confirmation that the remaining blocked vectors (Read tool, json.tool, etc.) are effective under real Codex behavior.
top_risks: Kimi provider bounding (tools=[], subagents={}, --final-message-only) remains validated only by dispatcher self-checks, with no independent agent invocation log proving the constraints hold in production.
Live Codex hook evidence covers only cat and python3 -c open(...); the broader self-check matrix (Read tool, json.tool) is unproven in live PreToolUse scenarios.
Metadata verification is enforced at dispatcher write time, but there is no evidence of a Cap-side gate rejecting metadata from older dispatcher versions, manual writes, or post-write tampering.
missing_evidence: Independent (non-dispatcher) Kimi CLI invocation demonstrating that tools=[], subagents={}, and --final-message-only actually suppress intermediate reasoning and tool use.
Live Codex PreToolUse test results for all self-checked blocked vectors, especially the host Read tool and python3 -m json.tool paths.
Cap consumption path automatically rejecting metadata files that lack the current dispatcher's verification stamp or were produced outside the verified write path.
minimum_fix: Before Cap relies on this as hardened infrastructure: (1) provide one independent Kimi agent run log proving the bounding flags work; (2) demonstrate live Codex blocking for the full self-check matrix (at minimum Read tool and json.tool); (3) ensure Cap's metadata consumer validates dispatcher version or verification epoch so stale or manually written metadata cannot be consumed.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Do not accept iterations that only expand self-check test cases or hook regexes. The loop stops only when independent Kimi validation and live Codex coverage of all claimed blocked vectors are provided.

user_intent_alignment: mostly aligned. The metadata verification and raw-read interception improvements directly serve the user's intent to prevent blind trust and context pollution. The gap on Kimi invocation independence prevents full alignment.
